item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q012_not_true_family_specific_pair","answer":"Their homology is not established by SCOPe 2.08. d1s9za_ (Amyloidogenic design-1; SUNID 98768) and d1hqja_ (Unnamed design-1; SUNID 61142) both belong to k.40.1.1, “Designed trimeric coiled-coil” (family SUNID 100905), but that family explicitly carries the annotation “not a true family.” Thus, their shared family code groups designed structures; it does not establish common evolutionary ancestry. The API’s generic family-level homology flag must be read with this specific caveat. Their shared superfamily k.40.1, fold k.40, and class k (“Designed proteins”) do not supply independent evidence of homology. Ordinary families and superfamilies imply evolutionary relationships at different strengths; fold or class membership alone does not. These two synthetic designs should therefore not be treated as demonstrated homologs, nor should amyloidogenicity or other functional properties be transferred between them from this classification. Establishing a relationship would require independent sequence and design-provenance evidence; structural resemblance alone is insufficient.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1s9za_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1hqja_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/98768","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/61142","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103786","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/64668","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103785","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100906","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100905","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100904","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100905/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100905/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/100905/homology"]}]}
